scope: All 46 South Carolina counties: five county tax-office sources individually reviewed; remaining county official websites listed for follow-up verification. Directory links are not proof of available overages.

legal_baseline.summary: After applying outstanding municipal tax liens, remaining overage belongs to the owner of record immediately before the end of the redemption period. Payable 90 days after execution of the tax deed unless another claimant institutes a judicial action during that time. Unclaimed/unassigned overage escheats five years after the public auction tax-sale date.
legal_baseline.important: The legal claimant is not a finder. County rules and documents may require identity proof, deeds, probate authority, notarization, or a court order. Never promise or claim entitlement.

docket_check_protocol: Use the official county Trial Court Public Index and select the correct county/court.
Search the case number or parcel/case reference from the official tax deed or court record; do not rely on a similar party name.
Review entries for motion/petition to claim surplus, objections, hearing notices, orders, appeal/stay, and disbursement/payment.
Open the filed order or contact the Clerk of Court to confirm the signed order and actual custodian balance.
Record the date checked, portal used, exact event/document title and result. 'No result' means unknown, not clear or available.
Do not automate around CAPTCHA, access controls, login gates, sealed records or paid subscriptions.
limits: This registry is a verified-source directory and monitoring checklist, not a statewide list of money owed. The bot cannot automatically determine entitlement or confirm current balances from these pages.

coverage_summary.meaning: All 46 county websites are listed. Forty-one counties have individually reviewed official delinquent-tax, tax-sale, overage or office sources; five remain county-portal entry points awaiting page-level review. Fairfield is the only county with a published historical overage listing located in this review (tax-sale years 2021–2024).
